questions.rationale: Correct answer: 600 mm square or 600 mm diameter. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1206.
questions.explanation: The length-based (not area-based) 25% calculation is the most misapplied detail in Sec. 1204. For an 18.00 m wall: 0.25 × 18 = 4.50 m total opening width is permitted. The two limits (25% of length and 10.00 sq.m single opening) operate independently — both must be satisfied simultaneously.

questions.text: How are vertical openings generally controlled under Section 1204?

options.text: They are enclosed according to the fire-resistive requirements of the construction type
They are left open if less than 2 storeys
They are governed only by plumbing code
They need no enclosure in any occupancy

questions.rationale: Correct answer: They are enclosed according to the fire-resistive requirements of the construction type. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1204.
questions.explanation: The occupancy-separation-based rating method makes PH shaft design more nuanced than the IBC story-count rule. An architect must first determine the occupancy groups of all floors served, determine the required separation hours between those occupancies (from Rule VI), and then use that separation rating as the enclosure rating. This requires cross-referencing Rule VI before applying Sec. 1204.

options.text: Approved ventilation to and through the main roof

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Approved ventilation to and through the main roof. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1204.
questions.explanation: Escalators create an open vertical chimney between floors that can spread fire and smoke within seconds. The draft curtain confines smoke at ceiling level while the sprinkler water curtain suppresses spread. The 'all sides' requirement for the curtain is a frequent trap — two sides is insufficient.

questions.text: Where must rubbish and linen chute openings not be located in non-Group A occupancies?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Required exit corridors or stairways. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1204.
questions.explanation: The 2-hour enclosure wall with 3-hour opening assembly is the opposite of what most candidates expect (usually, opening assemblies are rated lower than the wall). The logic: the wall provides the passive barrier while the door must match the full occupancy separation rating — the more active/vulnerable element must be rated higher.

questions.text: What is required of floors under Section 1205?

options.text: They must be framed and secured into the framework and supporting walls as an integral part of the whole building
They may be independent of supporting walls
They are governed only by room occupancy
They need no lateral buckling control

questions.rationale: Correct answer: They must be framed and secured into the framework and supporting walls as an integral part of the whole building. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1205.
questions.explanation: This requirement is frequently overlooked because engineers often treat lateral bracing as an NSCP matter. Section 1205 establishes the Building Code obligation — the NSCP then provides the specific bracing intervals and methods. The code-level mandate is in PD 1096; the engineering detail is in NSCP.

questions.text: What minimum attic access size is stated for combustible ceiling or roof construction?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 600 mm square or 600 mm diameter. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1206.
questions.explanation: The vertical projection application method is the standard wind engineering convention for determining wind force on a structure. It equals horizontal wind pressure × projected vertical area. Typhoon-prone regions in the Philippines (Visayas, Eastern Luzon, Bicol) regularly require design wind loads of 200–300 kg/sq.m per NSCP — well above the 120 kg/sq.m code minimum.

questions.text: How are vertical openings generally controlled under Section 1204?

options.text: They are enclosed according to the fire-resistive requirements of the construction type
They are left open if less than 2 storeys
They are governed only by plumbing code
They need no enclosure in any occupancy

questions.rationale: Correct answer: They are enclosed according to the fire-resistive requirements of the construction type. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1204.
questions.explanation: Under PH practice, a mixed Group E/Group H building with 3-hour occupancy separation triggers a higher shaft rating than a pure Group B building with 1-hour separation — regardless of building height. Under IBC, both would use 1-hour if the shaft serves ≤3 stories. This difference is a consistent LEA board exam topic on PH-vs-international code distinctions.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1204; IBC Sec. 713.4

options.text: Approved ventilation to and through the main roof

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Approved ventilation to and through the main roof. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1204.
questions.explanation: The draft curtain (passive containment) and sprinkler ring (active suppression) are a system — each addresses a different failure mode. The curtain prevents horizontal smoke spread before sprinkler activation; the sprinklers provide the water curtain after activation. Neither is optional. Two violations exist in this scenario.

questions.text: Where must rubbish and linen chute openings not be located in non-Group A occupancies?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Required exit corridors or stairways. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1204.
questions.explanation: This question tests the referral code relationship: PD 1096 sets the administrative minimum; the NSCP (a referral code under IRR Sec. 103) provides the engineering calculation that supersedes it whenever the engineering value is higher. PD 1096 and NSCP work in tandem — whichever produces the more demanding requirement governs.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1206; NSCP Chapter 2

questions.text: What is required of floors under Section 1205?

options.text: They must be framed and secured into the framework and supporting walls as an integral part of the whole building
They may be independent of supporting walls
They are governed only by room occupancy
They need no lateral buckling control

questions.rationale: Correct answer: They must be framed and secured into the framework and supporting walls as an integral part of the whole building. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1205.
questions.explanation: The three numbers must be memorized with their correct dimensional context: 200 mm is a depth (curtain hangs down from ceiling); 600 mm is a horizontal distance (from curtain face to sprinkler head); 1.80 m is a spacing interval (between adjacent sprinkler heads). Each describes a different geometric relationship in the escalator cross-section.
